newsitem.title: TURKEY: Further Turkish MP quits, Yilmaz nears majority.
newsitem.headline: Further Turkish MP quits, Yilmaz nears majority.

text.p: A further Turkish MP quit the pro-Islamist alliance on Friday, leaving secularist Mesut Yilmaz just one vote short of the majority his planned coalition would need to win a confidence vote, Anatolian news agency said.

"DYP (True Path Party) Istanbul deputy Tekin Enerem resigned from his party," state-run Anatolian reported. His resignation was the fourth from True Path and the fifth from its alliance with Islamists on Friday.

Parliament officials confirmed Enerem's resignation, which reduced the conservative True Path and their Islamist allies to 274 MPs on paper, compared with 273 deputies who are likely to back Yilmaz at a confidence vote on his left-right alliance.
Istanbul shares jumped over six percent on Friday on rising hopes that Yilmaz, a free-market conservative, can keep the Islam-based Welfare Party from returning to office.
Yilmaz was appointed prime minister-designate last week to replace Necmettin Erbakan, who resigned after a stormy year as modern Turkey's first Islamist prime minister.

Around a fifth of the True Path's deputies have quit since leader Tansu Ciller, under pressure from corruption charges, dropped strong criticism of the Islamists and joined Erbakan in government last year.
